answer: The raven multiplier is published, charged in relic, and vault lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 13 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, because the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 2564 identities would post 3464 proofs and burn roughly 11 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
